title: Geopolitical shocks are transmitting through trade, energy, finance, shipping, and unequal clean-investment capacity
source_unit: UN Trade and Development, Trade and Development Foresights 2026: Global economy faces a geopolitical challenge
geography: Global trade, investment, energy, shipping, industrial production, financial conditions, and developing-economy exposure

denominator.unit: world economy, merchandise trade, industrial production, and global investment frame

trade_growth_2025.unit: percent world merchandise trade growth in 2025

trade_growth_2026_projection.unit: projected world merchandise trade growth range for 2026

outlook_mechanism.value: geopolitical uncertainty weighs on trade, investment, supply chains, and growth after a stronger-than-expected start to 2026

observations.method: UN Trade and Development macroeconomic, trade, investment, and supply-chain analysis using global and national economic indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The 2026 trade figure is a projection range sensitive to conflict, policy, prices, shipping, and financial conditions; it is not a country-level forecast or household welfare estimate.
observations.subgroup: Developing economies, exporters and importers, workers in traded sectors, firms in global value chains, governments, and households exposed to price or employment shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trade can remain resilient through rerouting, inventory adjustment, services, and new partners even when aggregate merchandise growth slows; weak trade growth does not imply uniform recession.

denominator.unit: energy markets, financial conditions, maritime routes, and geopolitical-shock transmission frame

shock_channels.value: conflict in the Middle East disrupted energy markets, financial conditions, and major shipping routes

strait_of_hormuz.value: the Strait of Hormuz is identified as a critical route for global oil and gas trade

living_cost_channel.value: slower growth and rising living costs are among the report's central concerns

observations.method: UNCTAD analysis of geopolitical events, energy and shipping routes, financial conditions, and macroeconomic spillovers.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies transmission channels but does not estimate the causal effect of any single conflict on a particular household, firm, route, or price.
observations.subgroup: Energy-importing economies, shipping and logistics firms, consumers, workers, commodity producers, vulnerable countries, and public finance systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Route substitution, strategic reserves, demand adjustment, and policy intervention can moderate or redistribute the shock; disruption need not be permanent.

observations.period: 2024-2026; clean-energy investment and unequal productive capacity

denominator.unit: global solar-resource, clean-energy-investment, and energy-transition frame

renewables_cost_comparison.unit: percent of newly commissioned utility-scale electricity capacity comparisons in which renewables were cheaper than the cheapest new fossil alternative in 2024

africa_solar_resources.unit: percent of the world's best solar resources located in Africa

africa_clean_investment.unit: percent of global clean-energy investment received by Africa in 2024

capacity_gap.value: resource endowment and investment access are sharply misaligned

observations.method: UNCTAD comparison of utility-scale generation costs, resource geography, and global clean-energy investment flows.
observations.uncertainty: Cost comparisons depend on technology, financing, location, grid integration, and time horizon; investment shares do not measure delivered capacity, reliability, or local benefit.
observations.subgroup: Energy-poor communities, African economies, public and private investors, utilities, industrial firms, workers, and households exposed to energy costs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low generation cost can coexist with high financing, transmission, storage, or governance barriers; investment can rise without translating into affordable or reliable service.

denominator.unit: global AI investment, industrial production, critical-technology, and development-capacity frame

ai_investment.value: strong investment linked to artificial intelligence supported global industrial momentum entering 2026

industrial_policy.value: resilience requires stronger investment in clean energy and critical industrial components such as chips, batteries, and electric motors

dependency_question.value: technology and industrial concentration can strengthen growth while increasing exposure to supply, finance, and geopolitical dependencies

observations.method: UNCTAD synthesis of industrial production, AI-related investment, critical technologies, supply chains, and development policy.
observations.uncertainty: Aggregate investment momentum does not identify who captures productivity, wages, or control; the report does not establish causal employment or distributional effects of AI investment.
observations.subgroup: Developing economies, technology firms, industrial workers, public investors, suppliers of critical components, and communities exposed to transition costs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Technology investment can diversify productive capacity and create new work when skills, finance, competition, and public infrastructure are broadly available.

related_sources.claim: UNCTAD World Investment Report 2026 provides complementary evidence on concentrated investment, geopolitical uncertainty, and economic fragmentation.
UNCTAD Trade and Development Report series provides the longer-run development, trade, finance, and policy context.

boundary: This record adds a global trade, energy, investment, industrial-capacity, and geopolitical-shock route. It uses aggregate macro indicators, projections, investment comparisons, and report synthesis, not household price panels, firm-level supply-chain histories, causal AI employment estimates, or proof that clean-energy investment delivers local welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN Trade and Development Foresights 2026 materials were reviewed for the 2026 trade outlook, geopolitical transmission through energy and shipping, clean-energy investment concentration, and AI-linked industrial investment.
